plan.title: Mouse tumor immune/stromal composition: anti-PD-1 vs control
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 6 anti-PD-1-treated vs 6 isotype-control mouse subcutaneous tumors, raw gene-level Salmon counts (12000 genes x 12 samples), single batch, unpaired. sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median and per the grounded QC rule (R-0008/R-0030) must be kept and inspected, not silently dropped, since DESeq2's size factors already account for depth differences. The research question is descriptive/comparative composition (immune and stromal cell fractions per sample, treated vs control), not a DE question per se, so the core analytical work is deconvolution, routed to the immune-profiling-agent. Because this is mouse data, the knowledge service explicitly flags that human-trained deconvolution tools (MCP-counter, xCell, EPIC, quanTIseq, CIBERSORT) are invalid here (R-0136) — their marker sets and reference profiles are human-derived. The mouse tool of record, mMCP-counter, IS present in this environment (mMCPcounter R package, v1.1.0), so we use it directly rather than stopping or falling back to descriptive-only scoring. immunedeconv (present, v2.1.4) is also available and wraps mMCP-counter, seqImmuCC, DCQ and BASE for mouse — we use it as the primary interface since it standardizes cell type names and additionally gives cross-checks (DCQ, BASE) plus mouse-specific utilities. As a secondary cross-check we run ConsensusTME (present) in its mouse-adaptable ssGSEA/enrichment mode restricted to gene sets intersected with the mouse gene symbols in the matrix (ConsensusTME itself is human-derived gene sets, so this is reported strictly as a descriptive cross-check, not a validated mouse deconvolution, consistent with R-0136's caution). We also score PanglaoDB mouse-specific (Mm) marker gene sets per sample with UCell/singscore for stromal/immune populations (fibroblasts, endothelial, pericyte) that mMCP-counter's 16-population panel may not fully resolve, again as descriptive signature scores, not fraction estimates. Counts are converted to linear-scale TPM/CPM (gene lengths unavailable without transcript info from Salmon quant metadata, so CPM is used with this stated as a limitation) per R-0129 before any deconvolution/marker-scoring step — never log-transformed for the absolute/marker methods. Composition estimates and marker scores are compared treated vs control with a two-group test (limma or Wilcoxon given n=6 per group) per R-0134/R-0155-adjacent logic, with BH correction across the tested populations/signatures, and reported beside — never substituting for — a proper DESeq2 differential expression analysis (also included, since the research question implicitly invites checking whether compositional differences confound or explain any gene-level signal). QC step keeps sample_01 through vst(blind) PCA and sample-distance diagnostics and reports it explicitly rather than removing it by default.
